title: The Deadline of Vienna
premise: Odile Halloran, a whistle-blower living under four names, is hired to trace a vanished flight — a passenger jet that disappeared from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne. Following the erased trail through Vienna's archives and embassies, he discovers the flight carried evidence of a multinational cover-up, and that an assassin is eliminating everyone who remembers it existed. With three governments racing to bury the truth and dawn approaching, Odile must smuggle the recovered flight records to a journalist's extraction plane before the assassin finds him; he succeeds at the cost of burning his final identity, ending the book with Odile stepping onto the tarmac as no one at all — free, nameless, and finally honest.
about_author: O. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent eleven years inside European civil registries before leaving quietly and writing about what paperwork can hide. The Deadline of Vienna is their third novel, all written under names that are not quite their own.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a Vienna safe flat, we meet a man who changes identities like coats, working unattributable cases for clients who need deniability. A new commission arrives: find out why Flight 4471 has no record of ever existing — though it landed two hours ago. Beat: controlled loneliness cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: The Plane That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile interviews the ground crew chief, who swears the jet landed, then finds the man's employment history scrubbed overnight. POV shifts briefly to the crew chief's terror. Beat: first chill — the erasure isn't sloppy, it's total.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He reconstructs the passenger list from boarding-gate memory, hotel bookings, and a child's drawing left in seat 12C. One name recurs: a mid-level EU auditor who checked in but never checked out. Beat: the case acquires a human face.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Room
chapters.summary: Odile searches the auditor's hotel room, finding a hidden drive and signs of hurried departure — or abduction. Outside, a grey-eyed man watches from across the street. Beat: dread arrives; Odile realizes he's not the only hunter.

chapters.title: Grey Eyes
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. We see Vienna through a professional's patient eyes as he logs targets on a printed list — Odile's alias among them. He works methodically, almost tenderly. Beat: menace without malice; the reader knows what Odile doesn't.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. His client contact reveals fragments: Austrian, German, and French authorities each hold a piece of the flight's suppression order, each blaming the others. Beat: vertigo — the conspiracy has no center, only momentum.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Odile visits Marta, a retired registry archivist who keeps paper copies out of spite. She confirms the flight carried sealed diplomatic cargo — and that the auditor was its courier. Beat: warmth and warning; Marta becomes his one anchor.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. He eliminates the ground crew chief in a staged gas leak, unhurried, checking the man's pulse out of respect. Beat: cold horror; the stakes turn mortal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Running Out of Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Two of his four identities are compromised within hours; he burns them and moves safe houses. Loyalty to his handler wars with the truth he now carries. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Odile decrypts the auditor's drive: cockpit recordings and documents proving the three governments jointly ordered the flight's disappearance after the auditor threatened to expose arms shipments. Beat: righteous fury — the truth is worse than the crime.

chapters.title: Marta's Door
chapters.summary: Odile returns to warn Marta and finds her flat turned over, her card catalog burned. A neighbor saw grey eyes. Beat: grief and guilt; his anchor is gone because of him.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Odile contacts Lena Voss, an exiled investigative journalist with a dawn extraction flight arranged by a press foundation. She'll take the drive — if he can get it past airport security and whoever else knows. Beat: fragile hope, a plan with a clock on it.

chapters.title: Handler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's handler offers him a new identity abroad in exchange for handing over the drive to 'the right people' — meaning one of the three governments. Odile refuses, choosing truth over safety. Beat: loyalty vs. truth reaches its breaking point.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV. He intercepts Odile's courier route, kills the intermediary, and leaves the drive case behind — a message. But Odile had already swapped it. Beat: cat-and-mouse tightening; both men realize the other is smarter than expected.

chapters.title: Vienna After Midnight
chapters.summary: Odile moves through closed streets, sewers, and a night market to reach the airport district, trading his last clean identity for passage. Beat: exhaustion transfigured into purpose; the city itself feels complicit.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Odile talks his way past airport security using a dead man's credentials, while Lena waits airside. The assassin arrives at the terminal minutes behind him. Beat: breathless near-miss; the clock dominates.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Tarmac
chapters.summary: Climax. Assassin corners Odile between hangars; instead of fighting, Odile gives him the auditor's name and asks who he was before his own file was erased. The assassin hesitates — they are the same kind of ghost. Beat: recognition between enemies.

chapters.title: Dawn Departure
chapters.summary: The assassin lets Odile walk, then turns toward his employers' handlers with the drive's duplicate — his own quiet defection. Odile boards with Lena as the sun rises over the runway. Beat: release; mercy chosen over duty.

chapters.title: The Story Breaks
chapters.summary: Lena's POV en route. Over the Alps she files the story; within hours, ministers resign and inquiries open in all three capitals. Beat: vindication tempered by cost — justice arrived, but late and bloodied.

chapters.title: What the Records Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a safe house abroad, he reads the aftermath coverage and mourns Marta and the crew chief, understanding that exposure is not the same as repair. Beat: sober reckoning; victory without triumph.

chapters.title: No Name at All
chapters.summary: Odile destroys his remaining documents, keeping only the child's drawing from seat 12C. For the first time in years he introduces himself honestly to a stranger — with nothing but his face. Beat: quiet liberation; identity surrendered, self reclaimed.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Months later, a small press imprint publishes a novel about a vanished flight under a new pen name. In a Vienna café, grey eyes read the first page and smile faintly. Beat: cyclical grace — the truth survives by wearing whatever name it must.
